questions.question:
Which of the following is/are example(s) of cold-blooded animals?

I. Turtles

II. Snakes
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Cold-blooded animals:

__
 
• Cold-blooded animals are animals that are not capable of regulating their body’s temperature according to the temperature of the surrounding.
 
• They do not have a constant body temperature.
 
• Cold-blooded animals include reptiles, amphibians, fishes, insects, and other invertebrates.
 
• These animals are also called poikilothermic animals.
 
• Turtles and Snake both are cold-blooded animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Warm-blooded animals:

 
• Warm-blooded animals are the animals that are capable of maintaining a nearly constant body temperature irrespective of the temperature of the environment.
 
• Their body temperature remains the same as they move from one surrounding to another.
 
• The temperature control is mostly obtained by regulating their metabolic rates.
 
• Warm-blooded animals include birds and mammals.
 
• These animals are also called homeothermic animals.

questions.question:
Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by ________.

 a) an abnormally heavy body weight

 b) an intense fear of losing weight

 c) a distorted perception of weight

 d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**c and d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anorexia Nervosa is characterized by a **distorted perception of weight** and body image, where individuals see themselves as overweight despite being underweight.
 
• Individuals with Anorexia Nervosa often engage in **excessive exercise, extreme dieting, and other behaviors to lose weight**.
 
• This disorder involves an **intense fear of gaining weight** and a persistent behavior to avoid weight gain.
 
• People suffering from this condition may have a **low body mass index (BMI)** due to restricted food intake.
 
• Anorexia Nervosa can lead to severe health complications, including **malnutrition, bone loss, and heart problems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eating Disorders:** A range of psychological disorders characterized by abnormal or disturbed eating habits, including Anorexia Nervosa, Bulimia Nervosa, and Binge Eating Disorder.
 
• **Body Dysmorphic Disorder:** A mental health condition where a person spends a lot of time worrying about flaws in their appearance, which are often unnoticeable to others.
 
• **DSM-5 Criteria:** The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, outlines specific criteria for diagnosing Anorexia Nervosa, including restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, intense fear of gaining weight, and disturbance in the way one's body weight or shape is experienced.
 
• **Health Risks:** Anorexia Nervosa can lead to severe physical health issues, such as electrolyte imbalances, cardiovascular complications, osteoporosis, and amenorrhea.
 
• **Treatment Options:** Include psychotherapy, nutritional counseling, medical monitoring, and sometimes medications to address underlying mental health issues.

questions.question: Earthworm belongs to which group of animal kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Earthworm:

__
 
• It is a terrestrial invertebrate belonging to the phylum Annelida. 
 
• They are the common inhabitants of moist soil and feed on organic matter. 
 
• Earthworms have a tube-like arrangement or cylindrical-shaped and reddish-brown segmented bodies.
 
• It respires through its skin and has a double transport system made of coelomic fluid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Unique features of different phyla- 

 
 
• Porifera- also known as spores because they have pores.
 
• Coelenterata- also known as cnidaria because they have cnidoblasts.
 
• Ctenophora- also known as sea walnuts or comb jellies. And they have comb plates.
 
• Platyhelminthes- also known as flatworms because they have a flat body.
 
• Aschelminthes- also known as roundworms because the body has a circular cross-section.
 
• Annelida- Body segmentation
 
• Arthropoda- They have joint appendages.
 
• Mollusca- Body covered with a calcareous shell.
 
• Echinodermata- Water vascular system.
 
• Hemichordata- The body is made up of proboscis, collar, and trunk.
 
• Chordata- Notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve, and paired pharyngeal gill slits.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: A post-anal tail is present in Chordates.
Mollusca is the largest animal phylum.
Ctenophores are commonly known as sea walnuts.
Locust is an example of Arthropoda.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mollusca is the largest animal phylum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Phylum Mollusca

 
 
• Main features:
 
 
• The body is divided into a head and a muscular foot.
 
• The mantle is always present in it.
 
• The alimentary canal is well developed.
 
• Respiration takes place through gills or ctenidia.
 
• Blood is colorless.
 
• Excretion takes place through the kidneys.
 
• Example: Pila, Octopus
 
 
 
 
 
• ​Mollusca is **not** the largest animal phylum.
 
• The **largest phylum** in the animal kingdom is **Arthropoda**.
 
• A post-anal tail is present in Chordates.
 
• Ctenophores are commonly known as sea walnuts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Arthropoda**

__
 
• Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom.

 
• Constituting about 80% of the animal kingdom, Arthropoda__ is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom.
 
• Arthropoda is a phylum in the animal kingdom.
 
• Some important characteristics of this phylum are:
 
 
• Segmented bodies.
 
• Joined appendages.
 
• Open circulatory system.
 
 
 
• This phylum includes **locusts**, spiders, lobsters, termites, millipedes, insects, crabs, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics was used by Aristotle to classify animals?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Habitat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aristotle, known as the **"Father of Zoology"**, was one of the first scientists to classify animals systematically.
 
• He used the **habitat** of animals as a primary criterion for classification.
 
• According to Aristotle, animals could be grouped based on where they lived, such as in water, air, or on land.
 
• This classification system led to three broad groups:
 
 
• **Aquatic animals:** Animals that live in water, such as fish and whales.
 
• **Terrestrial animals:** Animals that live on land, such as lions and elephants.
 
• **Aerial animals:** Animals that live in the air, such as birds and bats.
 
 
 
• This system was a foundational concept in the study of zoology and helped in understanding the diversity of life forms.
 
• Although this method is now outdated, it laid the groundwork for modern biological classification systems, such as the Linnaean taxonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specialised organs**__

 __
 
• Specialized organs refer to body parts adapted for specific functions, such as the heart for pumping blood or lungs for respiration.
 
• While Aristotle noted some anatomical differences, his primary classification was not based on the presence or absence of specialized organs.
 
• Modern taxonomy, however, does consider organ specialization in classifying species.
 
 
 
• **Types of body cells**__
 __
 
• The differentiation of body cells, such as prokaryotic vs. eukaryotic cells, was not a concept known during Aristotle's time.
 
• This characteristic became relevant only after the discovery of the cell by **Robert Hooke** in the 17th century.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**__
 
 
• Photosynthesis is a process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.
 
• Since Aristotle focused on animals, photosynthesis was irrelevant to his classification system.
 
• However, this process plays a crucial role in the classification of plants in modern botany.

questions.question: Those organisms which take food synthesized by plants are called ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heterotrophs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Those organisms which take food synthesized by plants are called Heterotrophs.
 
• The term "heterotroph" includes organisms that cannot synthesize their own food and rely on complex organic substances for nutrition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phototrophic:**

 
 
• These are organisms that carry out photosynthesis to acquire energy.
 
• They utilize sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose – their energy source.
 
• This group includes most plants and some bacteria and protists.
 
 
 
• **Autotrophs:**
 
 
• Autotrophs are organisms that can produce their own food from the substances available in their surroundings using light (photosynthesis) or chemical energy (chemosynthesis).
 
• Examples include plants, algae, and some types of bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Saprotrophs: **
 
 
• These are organisms that feed on dead and decaying organic matter by secreting enzymes into the environment and breaking down the organic matter into smaller particles which they then absorb.
 
• Fungi and bacteria are common examples of saprotrophs (also called saprophytes or decomposers).

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT fall under Non-Chordates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertebrata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Non-chordates

 
 
• Non-chordates are animals **without **a notochord or backbone whereas chordates have the same. 
 
• Gill slits are not present in non-chordates since they breathe through the body surface or trachea.
 
• Post-anal tail is absent in the case of non-chordates whereas the heart is generally absent and if present, it will be dorsally or laterally placed.
 
 
 
• **Vertebrata:**
 
 
• It is also called Craniata, any animal of the subphylum Vertebrata, the predominant subphylum of the phylum Chordata.
 
• They have backbones, from which they derive their name.
 
• The vertebrates are also characterized by a muscular system consisting primarily of bilaterally paired masses and a central nervous system partly enclosed within the backbone.
 
• ​Notochord is present in the embryonic stage and is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult.
 
• Examples - Fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

questions.question: What do you call the body cavity that is lined by mesoderm?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Coelom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **coelom** is a body cavity that is completely lined by the **mesoderm**, the middle layer of embryonic tissue in triploblastic animals.
 
• This cavity is filled with fluid and provides a space for the development and suspension of internal organs, allowing them to grow and move independently of the body wall.
 
• Coelomates, or animals with a coelom, exhibit a higher level of structural complexity and specialization in organ systems compared to animals without a coelom.
 
• The presence of a coelom is a key characteristic of many higher animal groups, including **annelids, mollusks, arthropods, echinoderms, and chordates**.
 
• The coelom plays an essential role in functions such as **circulation, respiration, and waste elimination** by providing space for the development of complex systems like the digestive and cardiovascular systems.
 
• The coelom also acts as a cushion for internal organs, protecting them from mechanical shocks and injuries.
 
• It allows the body to have a more flexible and efficient movement due to its role in forming a hydrostatic skeleton in some organisms like earthworms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diploblasts**__

 __
 
• **Diploblastic animals** are organisms that develop from two embryonic germ layers: the **ectoderm and endoderm**.
 
• They lack a mesoderm, which means they do not develop a true coelom. Examples include **cnidarians** like jellyfish and corals.
 
• These organisms usually have a simple body structure and radial symmetry.
 
 
 
• **Radial Symmetry**__
 __
 
• **Radial symmetry** refers to a body plan in which any plane passing through the central axis divides the organism into identical halves.
 
• This type of symmetry is seen in animals like **cnidarians** (e.g., jellyfish) and **echinoderms** (e.g., starfish in their larval stage).
 
• It is associated with animals that have a sessile or free-floating lifestyle.
 
 
 
• **Triploblasts**__
 
 
• **Triploblastic animals** are organisms that develop from three embryonic germ layers: the **ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm**.
 
• They can be further categorized as **acoelomates (without a coelom), pseudocoelomates, or coelomates** based on the presence and type of coelom.
 
• Examples include most higher animals like **arthropods, mollusks, and vertebrates**.
